chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Abdullah from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about the sick person for whom the Jamarat are thrown. He said: 'He is carried to the Jamarat and the stones are thrown on his behalf.' I said: 'But he is unable to do that.' He said: 'He is left in his home and the stones are thrown on his behalf.' I said: 'And the incapacitated sick person, is circumambulation performed on his behalf?' He said: 'No, but he is circumambulated (carried around).'
And the Takbir after fifteen prayers in Mina is an emphasized Sunnah, and in the other cities after ten prayers. What indicates this is what he narrated:

key_terms.الْجِمَارُ: The Jamarat (pillars/stones) in Mina used for the ritual of stoning
key_terms.يُطَافُ بِهِ: Circumambulation performed for him (while he stays in place)

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for a sick person performing Hajj rituals like stoning the Jamarat and circumambulation?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* clarifies the fiqh of Hajj for the ill, distinguishing between those who can be carried to the Jamarat and those for whom the ritual is performed on their behalf, while correcting the misconception that Tawaf can be done on behalf of the incapacitated. It further establishes the confirmed Sunnah of reciting Takbir after fifteen prayers in Mina and ten in other camps, reflecting the practical ease (rukhas) granted to pilgrims in Shia jurisprudence.
